# Policy rules

`medallion lint` runs these over the specification before anything is generated.

| Rule | Severity | Requirement | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MED000` | high | A waiver must not be past its expiry date | Exceptions must be temporary. |
| `MED001` | critical | The specification must match its schema | Problems are reported together, not one at a time. |
| `MED002` | critical | Every reference must resolve | A dangling reference generates SQL that fails at deploy time. |
| `MED003` | high | Data flows bronze to silver to gold, with no cycles | Layer skipping and cycles make lineage and recovery ambiguous. |
| `MED004` | high | Bronze is raw, append-only text | Typing at ingestion turns source drift into pipeline failures; raw text survives it. |
| `MED005` | high | Silver is typed, validated and keyed | Silver is the trusted layer: every row has a key, a sequence and a reason to be there. |
| `MED006` | high | Gold is a documented aggregate at a declared grain | A gold table without a grain cannot be reconciled or joined safely. |
| `MED007` | critical | Personal data is masked and never reaches an unmasked column | A mask on the source is worthless if a derived column copies the raw value. |
| `MED008` | medium | Every table has an owner, a domain, a classification and a description | Unowned, undocumented data is where incidents go to wait. |
| `MED009` | high | Expectations are named, graded and refer to real columns | An expectation nobody can read or that checks nothing is false assurance. |
| `MED010` | high | Readers of a type 2 table select the current version | Joining all versions multiplies rows and double-counts. |
| `MED011` | critical | Expressions stay inside the portable subset | Spec text is spliced into SQL; the subset keeps it safe and means the same thing everywhere. |
| `MED012` | high | Access is granted to groups by role, least privilege | Individual grants and broad privileges are the usual audit findings. |
| `MED013` | medium | Identifiers are lower_snake_case | One convention keeps SQL, grants and docs predictable. |
| `MED014` | high | Classification never drops below what it is built from | A confidential source cannot become an internal table by being copied. |
| `MED015` | high | Names are unique and do not collide with generated tables | Each table also yields _validated and _quarantine tables; a clash overwrites data. |
